inputs.text: Even five months after the ceasefire was announced in Gaza, the airstrikes continue unchecked and the humanitarian crisis is only worsening, making life increasingly dark and harsh for the people on the ground. This is yet another manifestation of deep structural inequalities and historical patterns of injustice that have long failed to shield vulnerable communities from displacement and relentless violence. A 56-year-old father of five named Ahmed Baroud, now displaced in Deir al-Balah, captured it clearly: “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen.” We cannot blame those caught in the suffering. Instead, the priority must be confronting the root causes through institutional reform, social justice, and real protections for the families and workers trapped in this crossfire.

output.main_topic: Ongoing airstrikes and worsening humanitarian conditions in Gaza after the ceasefire announcement
subtopics: Calls for institutional reform and protections
